regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This chemotherapy is given before chemoradiotherapy to improve cancer control. Induction is the first stage of the planned pathway, and does not replace the later treatment.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Induction chemotherapy before concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced nasopharyngeal cancer.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Gemcitabine is converted inside cells into forms that disrupt DNA building blocks and DNA copying. It can affect normal blood-cell production as well as cancer cells. Cisplatin links strands of DNA, the instructions inside cells, making it harder for cancer cells to repair damage and divide. Healthy cells may also be affected. Kidney function, hearing, blood counts and nerve symptoms help the team decide whether the next dose is safe.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8, with cisplatin 80 mg/m² on Day 1, every 21 days for a maximum of 3 cycles. The NCCP plan starts chemoradiotherapy 21–28 days after Day 1 of the last induction cycle, subject to review and recovery. This is measured from the first day, not from Day 8 or the end of that cycle. The later regimen has its own prescription.
key_points: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8, with cisplatin 80 mg/m² on Day 1, every 21 days for a maximum of 3 cycles.
Day 1: full blood count, kidney and liver tests. Day 8: full blood count. Audiology is arranged when clinically indicated; extra tests depend on symptoms and results.

treatment_rationale.summary: This chemotherapy is given before chemoradiotherapy to improve cancer control. Induction is the first stage of the planned pathway, and does not replace the later treatment.
treatment_rationale.setting: Induction chemotherapy before concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced nasopharyngeal cancer.
factors: Disease site, stage, prior treatment, renal function, hearing, neuropathy, nutritional reserve and patient priorities.
alternatives: MDT-appropriate local and systemic treatments, supportive care and the option of declining treatment.
limitations: A randomised study of 480 patients compared this three-cycle induction approach followed by chemoradiotherapy with chemoradiotherapy alone. At three years, 85.3% versus 76.5% were alive without recurrence. Severe acute side effects were more frequent with induction (75.7% versus 55.7%). These group results do not predict your personal outcome.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Chemotherapy is given with radiation to improve control of cancer in the head and neck. Your team confirms that this particular four-day carboplatin schedule suits your cancer and health.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancer when cisplatin is unsuitable. Source eligibility specifically describes stage III/IV oropharyngeal cancer without distant metastases.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Carboplatin interferes with DNA repair and cell division. Its dose is calculated from kidney function. Blood counts can fall, including platelets that help stop bleeding. It is a different prescription from cisplatin. AUC is a prescribing target for drug exposure, not the number of milligrams in your bag; your clinical team calculates the dose using kidney function. Fluorouracil, often shortened to 5-FU, interferes with the building blocks used to make DNA and RNA, which cells need to grow. It runs through a vein over the prescribed hours. Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) is an enzyme that breaks it down. Testing for DPD deficiency before treatment reduces risk but cannot rule out every severe reaction.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Carboplatin 70 mg/m² each day on Days 1–4, with fluorouracil 600 mg/m²/day on Days 1–4, every 21 days for 3 cycles, only concurrently with radiotherapy. Chemotherapy is given only during radiotherapy. If radiation is interrupted, contact the team before the next chemotherapy dose. Radiation oncology sets the radiation visits and follow-up.
key_points: Carboplatin 70 mg/m² each day on Days 1–4, with fluorouracil 600 mg/m²/day on Days 1–4, every 21 days for 3 cycles, only concurrently with radiotherapy.

Before each cycle: full blood count, kidney and liver tests. Review weight, eating, drinking, swallowing, mouth symptoms, hands and feet. Kidney measurement and hearing tests follow the source and individual plan.
Chemotherapy is given only during radiotherapy. If radiation is interrupted, contact the team before the next chemotherapy dose. Radiation oncology sets the radiation visits and follow-up.

treatment_rationale.setting: Locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancer when cisplatin is unsuitable. Source eligibility specifically describes stage III/IV oropharyngeal cancer without distant metastases.
factors: Disease site, stage, prior treatment, renal function, hearing, neuropathy, nutritional reserve and patient priorities.
alternatives: MDT-appropriate local and systemic treatments, supportive care and the option of declining treatment.
limitations: The GORTEC 94-01 evidence cited by NCCP concerns four-day carboplatin 70 mg/m² plus fluorouracil with radiation in advanced oropharyngeal cancer. Its numerical outcomes should not be treated as an exact estimate for every head and neck site or for the separate carboplatin AUC 4 schedule.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Chemotherapy is given with radiation to improve control of cancer in the head and neck. Your team confirms the treatment aim and why carboplatin is suitable for your circumstances.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancer when cisplatin-based treatment is unsuitable.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Carboplatin interferes with DNA repair and cell division. Its dose is calculated from kidney function. Blood counts can fall, including platelets that help stop bleeding. It is a different prescription from cisplatin. AUC is a prescribing target for drug exposure, not the number of milligrams in your bag; your clinical team calculates the dose using kidney function. Fluorouracil, often shortened to 5-FU, interferes with the building blocks used to make DNA and RNA, which cells need to grow. It runs through a vein over the prescribed hours. Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) is an enzyme that breaks it down. Testing for DPD deficiency before treatment reduces risk but cannot rule out every severe reaction.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Carboplatin AUC 4 on Day 1, with fluorouracil 600 mg/m²/day on Days 1–4, every 21 days for 3 cycles, only concurrently with radiotherapy. exclusion_orientation: Relevant medicine hypersensitivity; check the current NCCP source and component-specific assessment rules.
Baseline ANC <1.5 ×10⁹/L, platelets <100 ×10⁹/L, bilirubin >1.5 ×ULN or known complete DPD deficiency.

premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the prescribed medicines for the active treatment day. The regimen is classified as high sickness risk.

DPD testing checks for an enzyme deficiency that can increase toxicity. Normal testing does not eliminate risk. Call urgently for chest symptoms or unusually early severe diarrhoea, mouth soreness or confusion.
Follow your unit’s oral-care plan. Tell the team early about mouth pain, weight loss, choking or difficulty eating and drinking. Dietetic and swallowing support can help.

Fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, persistent vomiting or inability to drink needs urgent oncology advice. Severe chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, collapse or a seizure is an emergency: call 112/999.
Bring prescription, non-prescription and herbal medicines. Check interactions, allergies and any changes with the oncology pharmacist.
Ask about fatigue, work, transport, caring responsibilities, emotional support and help with appointments.
